_meta.indication: MAVYRET is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with chronic HCV genotype 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 infection without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A), and for adult patients with HCV genotype 1 infection previously treated with a regimen containing an HCV NS5A inhibitor or an NS3/4A protease inhibitor (but not both).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), open-label, parallel-group, multicenter trial comparing 8- and 12-week GLE/PIB regimens.
pivotal_trials.population: Genotype 1, non-cirrhotic adults, treatment-naive or PRS treatment-experienced, with or without HIV.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SVR12 (sustained virologic response 12 weeks after end of treatment), the Agency's preferred primary endpoint for HCV.
pivotal_trials.result: SVR12 (reviewer ITT) was 99.1% (348/351) in the 8-week arm and 99.7% (351/352) in the 12-week arm; the 12-week regimen demonstrated superiority against a 91% pre-specified clinical threshold.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized (2:1), open-label, active-controlled (SOF/DCV), multicenter, non-inferiority (6% margin) trial with a third non-randomized 8-week GLE/PIB group.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SVR12; primary objective was non-inferiority of 12-week GLE/PIB versus SOF/DCV (6% margin), followed by test for superiority.
pivotal_trials.n: N=505 (GLE/PIB 12w n=233; SOF/DCV 12w n=115; GLE/PIB 8w n=157)
pivotal_trials.result: SVR12 was 95.3% (222/233) for GLE/PIB 12w, 96.5% (111/115) for SOF/DCV, and 94.9% (149/157) for GLE/PIB 8w; the 12-week regimen was non-inferior to SOF/DCV (difference -1.2%, 95% CI -5.6, 3.1, above the -6% margin).

key_safety: The most commonly reported adverse reactions (>10%) were headache and fatigue. Across pooled trials the most common adverse reactions (>=5%) were headache (13%), fatigue (11%), and nausea (8%); 80% of adverse reactions were mild (Grade 1).
target_moa: Fixed-dose combination of two direct-acting antivirals: glecaprevir, an HCV NS3/4A protease inhibitor (necessary for proteolytic cleavage of the HCV polyprotein), and pibrentasvir, an HCV NS5A inhibitor (essential for viral RNA replication and virion assembly).
modality: Small molecule (fixed-dose combination of two direct-acting antivirals)

boxed_warning.content: Risk of Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) reactivation in HCV/HBV coinfected patients undergoing or completing treatment with HCV direct-acting antivirals not receiving HBV antiviral therapy; some cases have resulted in fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, and death. Test all patients for current or prior HBV infection before initiating treatment.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected for the drug classes and there were no controversial issues.
